intro.title: Pseudo-classes :hover :focus :active
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive button that changes its appearance when a user interacts with it. You will learn the core concept of CSS pseudo-classes, which are special keywords that style an element based on its state. The main technologies involved are the :hover, :focus, and :active pseudo-classes to handle mouse hover, keyboard focus, and click interactions. By the end, you'll be able to create more dynamic and responsive web elements using these fundamental CSS selectors.
intro.usecase: Pseudo-classes like :hover, :focus, and :active are essential for creating intuitive, accessible user interfaces across modern web applications. In e-commerce sites, :hover reveals product details or color options on cards, while :focus guides users through checkout forms with clear visual feedback. Dashboard components use :active to indicate clicked buttons or toggled filters, and navigation menus rely on these states to show interactive affordances. Mastering these selectors allows developers to build polished, responsive interfaces that improve user experience and meet accessibility standards.
